newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Moderate gain seen on Dragonfield debut.
newsitem.headline: Moderate gain seen on Dragonfield debut.

text.p: Shares of leather garment maker Dragonfield Holdings Ltd are expected to post moderate gains in their debut on Thursday, with a low price/earnings (P/E) multiple providing an incentive to buy, analysts said.
"The P/E ratio of the stock of about eight times is relatively cheap compared with counterparts in which their P/E is about 20 times," said Alex Wong, research analyst at Dharmala Securities.
Wong said Dragonfield should offer investors a bargain among the leather garment companies tapping the China market.
Dragonfield offered 90 million new shares at HK$1.00 each in a public offering in Hong Kong. The 81 million shares available for public subscription were 67.6 times subscribed.
The issue price represents a P/E multiple of 7.91 times on a proforma fully-diluted basis.

Shares of leather garments group Peking Apparel International Group Ltd is trading at about 18 times P/E, Guangdong Tannery Ltd at about 24 times and China Elegance International Fashion Ltd at about 21 times.
But some analysts warned that short-term investors might take profit and switch to other upcoming public offerings, which might limit upside in Dragonfield's share price.
Dragonfield has a sales and distribution network of 150 outlets throughout China.

The company said the net proceeds would be used to fund expansion of production facilities, set up showrooms and offices in China and Eastern Europe, and increase processing capacity of dry cleaning services.
